title.en: Geography: Climate and Natural Vegetation of India

text.en: Raju felt a hot summer wind. "What decides India's climate?" he asked.

India generally has a tropical monsoon climate with marked regional differences. The four textbook seasons are winter, the hot season, the southwest monsoon and the retreating monsoon season. Factors affecting it are latitude, altitude, distance from the sea, the monsoon winds and relief.
The south-west monsoon brings most of India's rain between June and September. Tamil Nadu gets much of its rain from the north-east monsoon in October to December. Tropical cyclones can form over the Bay of Bengal and the Arabian Sea.
Natural vegetation includes tropical evergreen, deciduous, thorn, mountain and mangrove forests. Mangroves grow in deltas such as the Sundarbans, while the Western Ghats have evergreen forests. Forests are conserved to protect wildlife.

India is commonly described as having a tropical monsoon climate, with substantial regional differences. The textbook distinguishes winter, the hot season, the southwest monsoon and the retreating monsoon season.

text.en: Rain this afternoon is weather. The usual pattern of temperatures and rainfall across many years describes climate.

board.text: Weather is short-term; climate is long-term

text.en: Places farther north or south receive sunlight at different angles through the year. Latitude helps explain differences in temperature.

board.text: Latitude changes how sunlight reaches the land

text.en: A hill station can be cooler than a nearby plain at much the same latitude. Temperatures generally fall with elevation in the lower atmosphere.

board.text: Elevation can make nearby places cooler

text.en: Water heats and cools more slowly than land. A coastal place often has a smaller temperature range than a comparable inland place.

board.text: The sea moderates coastal temperatures

text.en: Moist air can cool as it rises over hills. The windward side often receives more rain, while the side beyond the hills can be drier.

board.text: Relief affects where rain falls

text.en: During the cool season, parts of northern India can receive rain or mountain snow from weather systems known as western disturbances.

board.text: Winter is generally cooler and drier

text.en: Temperatures rise before the southwest monsoon. Some regions experience hot dry winds, while some get local thunderstorms.

board.text: The hot season comes before the summer rains

text.en: Seasonal heating changes patterns of air pressure and wind. During the summer monsoon, moist winds reach India from over the ocean.

board.text: Monsoon winds change with the seasons

text.en: Moist winds from the Arabian Sea reach the Western Ghats. Rising air can produce heavy rain on their western slopes.

board.text: The Arabian Sea branch reaches the west coast

text.en: Moist winds from the Bay reach parts of eastern and northeastern India. The direction of the winds and local hills affect rainfall.

board.text: The Bay of Bengal branch supplies rain farther east

text.en: Air crossing the Ghats can lose some of its moisture. Drier air on the other side often brings less rain than on the windward coast.

board.text: A rain shadow can occur east of the Ghats

text.en: As the season changes, the southwest monsoon withdraws from different regions at different times. The change is not simultaneous throughout India.

board.text: The southwest monsoon withdraws by stages

text.en: During October to December, moist winds and systems over the Bay of Bengal bring rain to much of coastal Tamil Nadu.

board.text: Tamil Nadu has an important later rainy season

text.en: Cyclones are organised low-pressure storms over warm seas. They can bring strong winds and heavy rains when they reach the coast.

board.text: The Bay of Bengal can develop tropical cyclones

text.en: Rainfall and temperature help determine which plants can grow. Soil, elevation and exposure also influence vegetation.

board.text: Natural vegetation reflects local conditions

text.en: In very wet settings, trees do not all shed their leaves in one season. The Western Ghats and parts of the northeast contain evergreen forests.

board.text: Evergreen forests stay leafy through the year

text.en: Many trees shed leaves when water is less available. Leaf fall can help them limit water loss.

board.text: Deciduous forests lose leaves in a dry season

text.en: Small leaves, thorns and other features can reduce water loss. Thorn scrub occurs in some drier parts of India.

board.text: Thorn vegetation is adapted to dry regions

text.en: Lower slopes and higher slopes have different conditions. Different plant groups occur in different elevation belts.

board.text: Mountain vegetation changes with height

text.en: Mangroves tolerate salty or brackish conditions. Their roots help them survive in wet tidal soils such as those of the Sundarbans.

board.text: Mangroves grow in some tidal coastal habitats

text.en: A forest provides habitat and helps protect soil and water. Healthy mangroves can also help shelter some coastal areas.

board.text: Conservation protects more than trees

text.en: First compare rainfall and temperature. Then consider whether a local factor such as salinity or elevation changes which plants can survive.

board.text: Use climate to explain a vegetation pattern

problem.en: Why does coastal Tamil Nadu receive substantial rain in October–December?

text.en: Northeast monsoon winds can pick up moisture over the Bay of Bengal.

why.en: Wind reaching a coastal district from over the sea can bring moist air.

text.en: The moist air and weather systems over the bay can bring rain to the coast.

why.en: This makes October–December an important rainy season for coastal Tamil Nadu.

problem.en: Why is the western side of the Western Ghats often wetter during the southwest monsoon?

text.en: Moist winds from the Arabian Sea rise towards the hills.
Water vapour condenses, often giving heavier rain on the windward side.

why.en: The air on the other side may carry less moisture.

problem.en: Why can Chennai receive an important share of rain after September?

text.en: The northeast monsoon season follows the main southwest monsoon season.

why.en: The two seasons bring rain to different places at different times.

text.en: Moist winds and weather systems over the Bay can bring rain to the Tamil Nadu coast.

why.en: October–December rainfall matters along this coast.

problem.en: Which vegetation fits a salty tidal delta?

text.en: Look for plants adapted to brackish water and saturated soil.

why.en: A tidal delta can receive both river water and seawater.

text.en: Mangroves fit these conditions.

why.en: The Sundarbans is a major mangrove example.

prompt.en: A friend says The monsoon brings rain only from December. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: The south-west monsoon is June to September.
